_meta.indication: FIRDAPSE is a potassium channel blocker indicated for the treatment of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized discontinuation (withdrawal) study; after an open-label run-in optimal-dose phase, patients were randomized 1:1 to continue amifampridine phosphate or downtitrate to placebo, with the primary endpoint assessed on Day 14.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years of age with a confirmed diagnosis of LEMS (nerve conduction findings or positive anti-P/Q type voltage-gated calcium channel antibody test); taking an adequate and stable dose (30 to 80 mg per day) of amifampridine.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline to Day 14 in Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) score and Subject Global Impression (SGI) score.
pivotal_trials.n: 38 patients randomized to the double-blind period; the primary analysis (full analysis set) included 37 patients, 22 on placebo and 16 on amifampridine phosphate.
pivotal_trials.result: Both co-primary endpoints favored amifampridine: QMG difference in LS means -1.7 (95% CI -3.4, -0.0), p=0.0452; SGI difference in LS means 1.8 (95% CI 0.7, 3.0), p=0.0028.

nct_ctgov.title: A Phase 3 Study of Amifampridine Phosphate in Patients With Lambert Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS)

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized discontinuation study; patients on a stable dose were randomized to continue amifampridine or switch to placebo, with the co-primary endpoint assessed on Day 4.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with LEMS on a stable dose of amifampridine phosphate for at least 7 days; 9 of the 26 patients had also participated in Study LMS-002.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline (Day 0) to Day 4 in QMG score and SGI score.
pivotal_trials.result: Both co-primary endpoints favored amifampridine: QMG difference in LS means -6.54 (95% CI -9.78, -3.29), p=0.0004; SGI difference in LS means 2.95 (95% CI 1.53, 4.38), p=0.0003.

nct_ctgov.title: Phase 3 Study to Evaluate Efficacy of Amifampridine Phosphate in Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS)

key_safety: Most common (>10%) adverse reactions: paresthesia (62%), upper respiratory tract infection (33%), abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhea, headache, elevated liver enzymes, back pain (each 14%), hypertension and muscle spasms (each 12%). Seizures can occur (incidence ~2%).
target_moa: Amifampridine phosphate is a voltage-dependent potassium channel blocker that is thought to enhance neuromuscular transmission and improve muscle function by increasing the release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile was acceptable, the clinical trial designs were acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear.

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of the treatment of pediatric patients with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome age 6 to less than 17 years to the prescribing information.

description.text: Increased maximum dose from 80 mg to 100 mg for adults and pediatric patients ≥45 kg, and from 40 mg to 50 mg for pediatric patients <45 kg

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for an increase in the maximum dose of Firdapse. For adults (any weight) and pediatric patients (45 kg or more), the maximum dose will be increased from 80 mg to 100 mg. For pediatric patients weighing less than 45 kg, the maximum dose will be increased from 40 mg to 50 mg.

summary.text: Amifampridine phosphate (Firdapse), a new molecular entity, received a priority review as an orphan-designated drug for the treatment of LEMS in adults; orphan status was granted for LEMS on 11/12/2009, and the application was approved first cycle on 11/28/18 without an advisory committee meeting or accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Amifampridine phosphate, a new molecular entity, is proposed to be used for the treatment of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) in adults.
